# Forward Metric Definitions

Use these definitions for every analysis of Forward College admissions and marketing
data. If a request needs a metric that isn't here, say which property you chose and why,
and flag it for the Digital Team to confirm.

Items marked [confirm] are working definitions that the Digital Team hasn't signed off
yet. State them when you use them.

## Before you report any number

1. State the period, including whether it is one cycle, several cycles combined, or to date.
2. State the filter: market definition, cycle and stage.
3. Give the count and the group size behind every rate (for example 28 of 97).
4. When a number could differ from a HubSpot view, name the filter that explains the gap.
5. Separate what the data shows from a hypothesis. Label hypotheses.
6. Don't describe a pattern as reliable unless it holds in both complete cycles. Flag small samples.

## Dimensions

| Concept | Property | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Market | highschool_diploma_country | Always High School Country. Don't use nationality, residence or IP country. |
| Cycle | admissions_cycle_year | Values such as 24/25, 25/26, 26/27. Cycles run September to August. Always filter on cycle when comparing cycles: a date filter alone also pulls in contacts from the current cycle. |
| Self-reported channel | channel | What the student told us. It follows hear_about_forward. It is not paid attribution. |
| First visit | hs_analytics_source, hs_analytics_source_data_1, hs_analytics_source_data_2 | HubSpot Original Traffic Source. Campaign is in hs_analytics_source_data_1, keyword in hs_analytics_source_data_2. |
| Google brand vs non-brand [confirm] | hs_analytics_source, hs_analytics_source_data_1 | Brand search is any Google campaign with BRD in its name. Everything else is non-brand, including PMax and Demand Gen. PMax can also serve brand searches. |
| Programme chosen by applicant | bachelors_selection, bachelors_plus_selection, double_bachelors_selection, open_bachelors_selection | Used from Submitted Application through Invited to Interview. An applicant can choose several, so counts of choices are not counts of people. |
| Programme group | - | Groupings of programmes used for comparison. |
| Degree offered | admission_offer_degree_new | Filled from 25/26. A student can hold several offers. |
| Degree enrolled on | degree_name | The degree a student enrols on. |
| Financial aid status group | financial_support_request_statut | Measured among admits. Group the statuses as below. |
| Country targeted (spend) | - | Spend is recorded by country targeted. Students are by High School Country, so the two can differ a little. |

### Self-reported channel

- Report channels on both self-report and first visit. They overlap; many friends and family applicants first arrived on a paid search click.

### First visit

- First-visit labels changed between cycles; much of 24/25 sits under Other Campaigns, so paid social comparisons are rough.

## Funnel stages

A contact reached a stage if its stage entry date is not null. Use the lifecycle date, not deal properties. In particular, Invited is defined by the lifecycle stage date.

| Stage | Lifecycle value | Entry date property |
|---|---|---|
| Started Application | 735800774 | hs_v2_date_entered_735800774 |
| Started Qualified | marketingqualifiedlead | hs_v2_date_entered_marketingqualifiedlead |
| Submitted Application | salesqualifiedlead | hs_v2_date_entered_salesqualifiedlead |
| Eligible Submitted Application [confirm] | 845219062 | hs_v2_date_entered_845219062 |
| Invited to Interview | opportunity | hs_v2_date_entered_opportunity |
| Admitted | 845292228 | hs_v2_date_entered_845292228 |
| Enrolling (accepted the offer) | 735815160 | hs_v2_date_entered_735815160 |
| Enrolled | 735815354 | hs_v2_date_entered_735815354 |

## Terms

- **Rejected:** The Admissions Status value "Unqualified" is labelled Rejected. Call it Rejected.
- **Offer accepted vs enrolled:** Offer accepted (Enrolling) is not enrolled. Use the Enrolled date for enrolment.
- **Cycle:** An admissions cycle, September to August, written like 25/26.
- **Market:** A student's High School Country.

## Metrics

### Contacts reaching a funnel stage (`stage_count`)

Number of contacts who reached a given funnel stage in the period.

- **Formula:** Count of contacts where the stage's entry_date_property is not null
- **Parameter:** stage (any funnel stage)
- **Time anchor:** The stage's entry_date_property
- **Filter:** Filter on admissions_cycle_year for the cycle(s) reported
- **Unit:** contacts
- **Slice by:** market, cycle, channel_self_reported, first_visit_source, google_search_type, programme_choice
- Offer accepted is not enrolled. Some students accept and never enrol, so use the Enrolled stage date for enrolment, not Enrolling.
- Programme choice counts are choices, not people (an applicant can choose several).

### Yield (`yield`)

Share of admitted students who enrolled.

- **Formula:** enrolled ÷ admitted
- **Time anchor:** Stage entry dates, within the cycle
- **Period:** Only quote it for complete cycles.
- **Unit:** percent
- **Slice by:** market, cycle, programme_group, enrolled_degree
- **Benchmark:** all_countries (see Benchmarks)

### Offers declined (`offers_declined_rate`)

Share of admitted students who declined their offer.

- **Formula:** offer_proposal = Offer Declined ÷ admitted
- **Time anchor:** Admitted entry date, within the cycle
- **Unit:** percent
- **Slice by:** market, cycle, programme_group, offer_degree
- **Benchmark:** all_countries (see Benchmarks)

### Spend per enrolled (`spend_per_enrolled`)

Paid spend in a market divided by everyone enrolled from that market.

- **Formula:** all paid spend in the market ÷ everyone enrolled from it, unless a channel is specified
- **Time anchor:** Spend by cycle; Enrolled entry date
- **Unit:** eur_per_contact
- **Slice by:** market, cycle
- **Benchmark:** spend_markets (see Benchmarks)
- Students are by High School Country and spend is by country targeted, so the two can differ a little.
- When a channel is specified, use that channel's spend only. Whether the denominator then becomes that channel's enrolled students isn't defined yet, so say which you used and flag it.

### Aid offer rate (of everyone who asked) (`fa_offer_rate_of_askers`)

Of admits who asked for financial aid, how many ended up with an offer.

- **Formula:** offered ÷ asked
- **Unit:** percent
- **Slice by:** market, cycle
- **Benchmark:** all_countries (see Benchmarks)
- Always report alongside fa_yes_rate_of_decided; they answer different questions.

### Aid yes rate (of decisions made) (`fa_yes_rate_of_decided`)

Of the students we made an aid decision on, how many we said yes to.

- **Formula:** offered ÷ (offered + refused)
- **Unit:** percent
- **Slice by:** market, cycle
- **Benchmark:** all_countries (see Benchmarks)
- Always report alongside fa_offer_rate_of_askers.

### Share of applicants choosing a format (`format_choice_share`)

Share of applicants who chose a given programme format.

- **Formula:** (total applicants − Unassigned in that field) ÷ total applicants
- **Unit:** percent
- **Slice by:** market, cycle
- **Benchmark:** all_countries (see Benchmarks)
- Fields are bachelors_selection, bachelors_plus_selection, double_bachelors_selection and open_bachelors_selection.
- Shares across formats can sum to more than 100%, because applicants can choose several.

- **Net revenue (tuition minus aid):** Can't be calculated from HubSpot yet, because aid amounts are missing for most of 24/25. It needs Finance's figures. Don't estimate it. [confirm] tuition_fees_personal_area is free text in mixed formats, and fee levels haven't been mapped to degree format.

## Sources

- **HubSpot CRM (contacts):** Funnel stages and dates, market, cycle, channel, first visit, programmes, offers, financial aid status.
- **Paid media and school visits spend sheet:** Paid spend by Google, Meta and school visits, by country targeted. Meta figures come from Meta Ads Manager, not the old sheet's numbers.
- **Finance:** Tuition and aid amounts, net revenue.

## Comparing cycles

- Same-date comparison: count each cycle up to the same calendar date using the stage date. For the current cycle, compare to the same date in earlier cycles.
- Remember a contact only appears in a cycle if it is tagged to that cycle now.

## Benchmarks

- **All countries:** Rates such as yield, offers declined, aid share and programme mix compare with all countries for the same cycles.
- **Markets we spend in:** Spend per enrolled compares with markets with at least €5k of spend across 24/25 and 25/26. Refresh the list when new cycle spend is added. In 24/25 and 25/26 these are Germany, Italy, United Kingdom, Spain, United States, Canada, France, Norway, Sweden, Brazil, Netherlands, Austria, United Arab Emirates, Portugal, Belgium, Finland, Colombia, Denmark, Mexico, Switzerland, Poland, Israel, Turkey, Morocco.
- All-country and spend-market benchmarks can tell different stories (Germany's yield is near the all-country figure but below the spend-market figure), so be clear which one is used.

## Data limits and market context

- The funnel exists from 24/25. 23/24 has enrolled counts only. Don't describe this as three years of funnel data.
- First-visit labels changed between cycles: much of 24/25 sits under Other Campaigns, so paid social comparisons are rough.
- Applicants from Nigeria, Pakistan and India are organic. Paid media is geo-targeted to chosen countries.
- Spain's 25/26 growth came from free press around the Princess of Spain enrolling. Don't treat it as repeatable.
- Faster time to invite isn't automatically better. Some delay signals exclusivity and demand.

## HubSpot query limits

- query_crm_data groups by at most two dimensions and silently drops a third. Filter on one dimension instead.
- Check every result for a note saying rows or dimensions were dropped.
- Column order in the result can vary, so read the header.
- OR conditions work in WHERE, which allows a per-cycle date filter in one query.
- Group by high-cardinality text fields only within one market, or the query can fail.
